messages:
Renee Park: Quick sync - ACME SI asked about how we handle marketplace entitlements when partners report usage in different billing granularity (minutes vs hours). They want guidance before they build their sidecar.
Omar Sheikh: Core question: do we normalize partner units to our canonical marketplace unit at ingest (e.g., minutes -> hours rounding/up/down) or keep native units and convert at billing aggregation?
Bianca Ruiz: Finance preference: normalize on ingest to avoid floating rounding issues later. But must record original_units and conversion_factor for audits.
ACME SI: We prefer to send usage in minutes (device-level), since that's what firmware reports.
Renee Park: Proposal: ingest path will accept a unit field and a partner_unit enum. Conversion rules: partner_unit -> marketplace_unit with rule {scale:float, method:ceil|floor|round}. Default mapping: minutes -> hours with scale=1/60 and method=ceil for GPU-minute to hour billing.
Omar Sheikh: Implementation sketch: POST /v1/partner-usage accepts body entries with fields: event_id, timestamp_iso, partner_sku, units, partner_unit, customer_id, metadata. Ingest pipeline will compute canonical_units = apply_conversion(units, mapping). We persist: original_units, canonical_units, conversion_method, conversion_factor.
Bianca Ruiz: Important: conversion_method must be contract-level agreed. Finance wants default ceil for minute->hour to avoid underbilling but partner can opt for round with signed contract amendment.
LedgerBot: Automated policy: for partner-reported granularity finer than marketplace_unit, ingestion will emit a `conversion_audit` record and include conversion metadata in the daily reconciliation artifact. Dry-run alerts if >0.2% variance introduced by rounding.
Renee Park: Edge case: partners that report in bursts (e.g., many tiny events per device) may create lots of duplicates if dedupe is per-device+minute. We will keep event_id dedupe canonical. If partner can't provide UUIDs, they must compute stable event_id as sha256(device_id + timestamp_iso + partner_sku). Document this in onboarding.
ACME SI: For bulk files we'll include manifest, sig as discussed earlier. Any change in conversion rules requires a new mapping version and effective_from date. How do we handle retroactive mapping fixes?
Omar Sheikh: Retroactive fixes: allow a backfill job that tags affected rows with mapping_version and replay_id, recomputes aggregates for the affected day ranges, and emits a `recalc` reconciliation report. Backfill policy: partner can request up to 90 days; anything older requires finance approval.
Bianca Ruiz: Audit artifacts required: original manifest + signature, sample first/last 10 rows, conversion_summary (rows changed by conversion, total original_units vs canonical_units), reconciliation_delta_per_sku. Retain all artifacts 400 days.
Renee Park: Sample partner payload snippet for docs: ```
POST /v1/partner-usage
Headers: X-Partner-ID: acme-si
[
  {"event_id":"e-abc123","timestamp_iso":"2026-03-20T10:12:00-07:00","partner_sku":"ACME_GPU_MINUTE","units":45,"partner_unit":"minute","customer_id":"cust-42"}
]
```
Response example: ```
{"accepted":1,"duplicates":0,"conversion_notes":["45 minute -> 1 hour (ceil)"]
```
Omar Sheikh: Error samples to include in spec: ```
400 {"error":"invalid_unit","detail":"partner_unit 'ticks' unknown"}
409 {"error":"event_duplicate","detail":"event_id e-abc123 already processed"}
```
Bianca Ruiz: Action items: Renee will draft conversion mapping table (CSV) and examples; Omar will add conversion metadata to ingest schema and wire in `conversion_audit` events; LedgerBot will include conversion impact threshold in dry-run checks. Renee will coordinate with ACME SI on preferred default (ceil vs round) and get written confirmation.
ACME SI: We'll send sample minute-level payloads next week. Thanks - we'll sign the conversion appendix if needed. :thumbsup:
